subject: Residency & operational 'no-learning' — questions and redlines
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@orbitalhealth.com>, legal@orbitalhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Residency and 'no-learning' confirmation needed before pilot

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile.

Before we move our pilot to a small group of clinicians, Legal needs a couple of clarifications around data use and residency:

- We need a clear statement that customer inputs/responses will not be used to train Redwood models (a firm operational "no-learning" commitment for our account, not just a promise to evaluate).
- If you can’t give a model-level no-train guarantee, can you confirm whether an onshore KMS + EU/US residency lane is available for our tenant?
- We also request a short exportability clause for our outputs (our compliance team wants to be able to extract transcripts and derivative outputs on reasonable notice).

Legal has a few redlines they typically send back; attaching our standard DPA for reference. Can you confirm what evidence you can provide and whether Redwood would accept the proposed redlines, or suggest acceptable alternative language?

Attachments: Orbital_DPA_Standard.pdf (PDF, 68KB)

Best,
Emma Stone
Head of Procurement — Orbital Health
emma.stone@orbitalhealth.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma.stone@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and 'no-learning' confirmation needed before pilot

Hi Emma,

Appreciate the clear list — and glad the demo was useful. Quick answers up front, with detail below:

1) Operational no-learning: Redwood can commit to an "operational no-learning" mode for a tenant when requested. That means we will not use customer inputs or generated outputs to improve or update any general models or training datasets; we also segregate logs subject to the tenant retention policy.

2) Onshore KMS + residency: We can provide an onshore KMS option (US-only) and a US residency lane for data at rest and processing within our US region. For EU residency we have a separate private deployment offering — we can scope that if needed.

3) Output exportability: We can add a contractual exportability clause permitting Orbital to extract transcripts and derived outputs on request; we typically include a process and SLA for export.

I attached a marked-up copy of Redwood's standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_marked.pdf) and a short processing footprint CSV that maps subprocessors and data flows.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Loop in Privacy (David Kim) for the proposed clause language; 2) If Legal wants to redline our DPA, please send back a tracked doc so we can review. Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate the procurement steps and timeline.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_marked.pdf (PDF, 92KB), processing_footprint.csv (CSV, 14KB)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@orbitalhealth.com, Emma Stone <emma.stone@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and 'no-learning' confirmation needed before pilot

Laura,

Thanks for the quick response. Legal reviewed your marked DPA and we’ve pulled a couple of non-negotiables:

- Orbital requires an explicit contractual prohibition on using customer data to train models that could be served to other customers. The phrasing we typically accept is "Customer Data will not be used to train, fine-tune, or update any models used for serving third parties."
- We also want assurance that any temporary cache or KV data that could be persisted for optimization is either disabled or fully tenant-isolated and deletable on demand.
- If Redwood cannot accept the model-level prohibition, we are open to a narrowly scoped operational commitment plus a technical attestation and a 3rd-party audit window.

I've attached our redlines (Orbital_DPA_redlines.docx). For now we flagged sections on Training, Subprocessors, and Exportability.

Can you confirm whether Redwood would:
A) Sign the explicit model-level prohibition as-is (preferred by us), or
B) If not A, provide a description of the operational controls + an attestation document and an option for the regional/private deployment that would achieve the same protections?

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Senior Counsel — Orbital Health
samir.rao@orbitalhealth.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@orbitalhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and 'no-learning' confirmation needed before pilot

Hi Samir / team,

Thanks for the clear redlines. I wrote up an operational position and proposed clause below — happy to jump on a call to walk through details and provide technical attestation.

Short position: Redwood can accept a contractual commitment that we will not use Customer Data to train or update any models that are shared with other customers (we call this a model-level ban). We offer two implementation paths depending on risk appetite:

Path A (preferred for Orbital if you need the strongest contractual protection):
- For your tenant we will enable a tenant-isolated serving stack and a private model snapshot used only for your account, deployed under Redwood Dedicated or Private.
- We will configure an onshore KMS for key material and ensure all persistent storage and inference occurs in the US region.
- Subprocessors: we will supply an up-to-date subprocessor list and can agree to a subprocessors change notice and approval process for any changes that would touch customer data.

Path B (operational no-learning + attestation):
- We will run the tenant on our hosted tier but enable operational controls: disable model improvement pipelines for your tenant, disable cross-tenant KV cache sharing, and enforce immediate retention/deletion policies for transcripts and ephemeral contexts.
- Redwood will deliver a quarterly attestation (signed) describing controls and a one-time 3rd-party audit report scope if you request it.

Proposed clause (plain text to consider including in the DPA):
"Redwood agrees that Customer Data, as defined in this Agreement, will not be used to train, fine-tune, or update any machine learning models that are made available to other customers. For avoidance of doubt, this prohibition includes use in any production model pipelines, training corpora, or model parameter updates. Redwood will implement the technical and operational controls necessary to ensure compliance with this commitment for the Customer's tenant, including but not limited to tenant isolation, onshore key management, and disabling cross-tenant caching. Redwood's obligations under this section are subject to the technical constraints identified in the annex (NoLearn_Operational_Definition.txt), and Redwood will provide a written attestation of controls on request."

Attachments I can provide immediately: the NoLearn_Operational_Definition.txt (detailed controls), an extract of our current subprocessors, and a draft subprocessor notice process. If you want Path A, Marissa can scope the Dedicated/private deployment options and costs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Orbital to confirm A vs B.
2) If B, we will provide the attestation and schedule the audit scope.
3) If A, Marissa will draft the Dedicated deployment SOW and timelines.

Happy to set up a short call with engineering and legal to close language this week.

-David
David Kim
Head of Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwoodinference.com
